newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast crudes firm on WTI, ANS sold on formula - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast crudes firm on WTI, ANS sold on formula - Oct 8.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices eased from midday but stayed up compared to Monday, with a cargo of Alaskan crude sold on a "formula" basis.
November West Texas Intermediate (WTI) closed 20 cents above Monday levels, helped by refinery buying after a tropical storm shut in some U.S. Gulf Coast production overnight.
Higher WTI prices lifted Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude prices by 20 cents to $23/23.30 a barrel.
The discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $2.30 a barrel less November West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
One large West Coast refinery sold ANS on a formula basis to another PADD 5 refiner. A formula price is determined by the average cost of WTI over several days or weeks.
A deal also got done on Monday for high-viscosity high-sulphur blend crude, a type of Outer Continental Shelf blend which moves down California's Line 63 pipeline.
The deal was struck at postings plus $4.60 a barrel.
Straight Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
